Student Performance Analysis | Synthetic sample data
Page 1
 STUDENT PERFORMANCE
 ANALYSIS
 A sample report for PDF parsing, chart extraction, table extraction, and RAG pipeline
 testing
Purpose
This report demonstrates how student exam scores, study hours, subject-level averages, and attendance can be
organized into readable text, structured tables, charts, and a process diagram. All numbers in this document are
synthetic and are intended only for software testing and demonstration.
Report contents
1. Dataset overview and field definitions
2. Descriptive statistics and score histogram
3. Subject comparison bar chart
4. Attendance and study-time analysis
5. Data table for extraction testing
6. Analysis workflow flowchart
7. Findings, limitations, and recommendations
Important: This report does not describe real students and should not be used to make decisions about any individual learner.

Student Performance Analysis | Synthetic sample data
Page 2
1. Dataset Overview
The sample dataset represents 50 fictional student exam scores on a 0–100 scale. Supporting summary values
are included to test whether a PDF parser can recover headings, paragraphs, table headers, numeric values, and
units. The report uses illustrative aggregate values rather than records about identifiable students.

Data interpretation note
The subject averages, attendance groups, and study-hour comparisons are separate illustrative summaries. They
are not computed by joining all measures for each fictional student. This distinction matters when interpreting
charts or testing extraction consistency.

Student Performance Analysis | Synthetic sample data
Page 3
2. Exam Score Distribution
A histogram groups numeric scores into intervals and shows how many observations fall into each interval. It is
useful for examining the spread, concentration, and possible skew of exam results.
Summary statistics for the 50 synthetic scores: mean = 74.7, median = 76.5, minimum = 42, maximum = 98, and
sample standard deviation = 14.1.
How to read the histogram
The horizontal axis shows score intervals from 40 to 100. The vertical axis shows the number of students in each
interval. A taller bar means more scores fall in that range. These values are generated for demonstration and do
not represent a school, exam board, or actual cohort.

5. Student Performance Analysis Workflow
A repeatable analysis process starts with data collection and validation, then summarizes outcomes and identifies
areas where additional support may be useful. The diagram below is an embedded vector graphic in the PDF, so it
provides a non-photographic visual element for parsing tests.
Collect student data
Clean and validate data
Analyze scores & attendance
Identify support actions
Suggested quality checks
 Confirm that scores are numeric and within the expected 0–100 range.
 Check for missing values and duplicate rows.
 Verify category labels such as subject and attendance group.
 Review whether aggregate tables use consistent denominators.
 Preserve source page numbers when extracting content from PDF.
Potential support actions
A real institution might investigate whether students need additional practice, attendance support, clearer learning
materials, or access to tutoring. Any intervention should be based on validated data and contextual review, not on
this synthetic report.

Glossary
Histogram: A chart that groups numeric values into intervals.
Bar chart: A chart comparing values across categories.
Attendance percentage: The share of scheduled sessions attended.
Embedding: A numeric vector representing text or other content for similarity search.
Chunk: A smaller segment of content created from a longer document.
Metadata: Supporting information such as page number, content type, or source path.

Student Performance Analysis | Synthetic sample data
Page 8
7. RAG Pipeline Testing Notes
This PDF is designed as a small, multi-format test fixture for a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflow. It
includes selectable text, multiple tables, a raster histogram, a raster bar chart, and a vector flowchart.
Recommended validation checklist
1. Extract paragraphs and headings, preserving page numbers.
2. Extract tables and confirm that each header remains associated with the correct values.
3. Confirm that the histogram and bar chart are detected as picture regions if the parser supports picture
extraction.
4. Extract or render the vector flowchart; note that vector graphics may not be represented as a conventional
embedded bitmap image.
5. Chunk extracted text and table Markdown without losing metadata.
6. Generate embeddings for text chunks and store them in ChromaDB.
7. Verify that the stored record count matches the number of submitted chunks.
